title: Ravenna
subtitle: Gateway to the Adriatic
summary: Ravenna marked the transition between our time on land and the beginning of our Mediterranean cruise. Known for its remarkable mosaics and deep history, the city gave us one final glimpse of Italy before we boarded Explorer of the Seas.
homepageSummary: Discover Ravenna's remarkable mosaics, quiet historic center, and its role as the gateway to our Mediterranean cruise.

quote.text: Ravenna felt like the pause between two adventures—the end of our Italian journey on land and the beginning of our time at sea.

facts.label: Known for
facts.value: Byzantine mosaics and early Christian monuments

facts.label: Historic connection
facts.value: Final resting place of Dante Alighieri

highlights.title: Byzantine Mosaics
highlights.description: Ravenna is renowned for richly detailed mosaics preserved inside churches and historic monuments.

highlights.title: Basilica of San Vitale
highlights.description: One of Ravenna's most important landmarks, known for its architecture and extraordinary sixth-century mosaics.

highlights.title: Dante's Tomb
highlights.description: The modest tomb of the author of the Divine Comedy connects Ravenna to one of Italy's most important literary figures.

highlights.title: Cruise Embarkation
highlights.description: Ravenna served as the gateway to the Adriatic and the beginning of our seven-night cruise.

tips.title: Confirm cruise transportation early
tips.description: The cruise terminal is outside Ravenna's historic center, so transportation should be planned before embarkation day.

tips.title: Allow time for the mosaics
tips.description: Several major mosaic sites are located throughout the city, and seeing more than one provides a fuller understanding of Ravenna's history.

tips.title: Stay near the historic center
tips.description: A central hotel makes it easier to explore Ravenna on foot before traveling to the cruise terminal.

tips.title: Treat Ravenna as more than a port
tips.description: Even a short visit can reveal important art, architecture, and history beyond its role as an embarkation city.
